thesis: OLAELEC and NETWEB did not share a fixed 0.5% RANGEBOUND stop. OLAELEC had a dynamic 0.395% stop at INR 40.37 and exited only after two consecutive completed five-minute candles closed beyond it; the live exit price was INR 40.25, making the gross loss 0.691%, and INR 117.76 of charges increased the net loss to 0.750%. NETWEB had a tighter dynamic 0.25% stop at INR 4,998.57. It recorded only one stop-confirmation bar before its management candle history jumped 95 minutes from 11:30 to 13:05 IST. At the next usable update, the time-stop signal-deterioration rule returned an exit at INR 4,924.50 before the stop check ran, producing a 1.728% gross loss and 1.813% net loss after INR 80.51 charges.

effectiveExitControls.description: Number of consecutive completed candles beyond the stop required to confirm a normal stop exit.
Minutes after entry during which normal stop checks are softened unless emergency conditions occur.
Hard adverse move percent from entry that can exit immediately, even during stop grace.
Modeled slippage used by cost estimates; confirmed-stop execution records the observed live management price rather than forcing the planned stop price.

limitations: This is analytics-reviewed only. No Replay, backtest, sweep, or targeted settings trial was run.

The stored NETWEB candles prove a 95-minute management-data gap, but the Advisor evidence does not identify whether the upstream cause was Sharekhan delivery, cache refresh, or candidate construction.

The source path checks signal deterioration before the final long-side stop check, so NETWEB's next candidate was classified by signal deterioration before the stop counter could consume that candidate.

The 0.5 values visible in RANGEBOUND configuration are not a fixed stop-loss: position sizing is 0.5, maximum tolerated Nifty decline is 0.5%, and gain milestones include 0.5%. RANGEBOUND stop distance is dynamic and stored per trade.
